quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 15 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best way to stay close together while keeping safe distance?

options.text: In pairs.
In a staggered formation.
In a single-file line.
In a passing formation.

questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets riders stay close while keeping safe space between them. Use single-file when riding through curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side with another rider.

questions.question: Alcohol does not need to be digested. What does this mean?

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts affecting the drinker right away.
The body never removes alcohol.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts affecting the drinker right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested, so it enters the bloodstream quickly and reaches the brain within minutes. Your body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: The effects can be stronger than when using either one alone.
The effects are less dangerous than when using either one alone.
The effects are usually small.
The effects usually cancel each other out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects can be stronger than when using either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make it harder to ride safely. Some drugs become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power does the front brake provide?

options.text: About one-quarter
About one-half
About three-quarters
All the stopping power

questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Get off the roadway.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle tailgaters is to change lanes and let them pass. Riding faster may only make it worse by letting them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all crashes?

options.text: They happen at speeds greater than 35 mph.
They happen at night.
They are caused by worn tires.
They involve riders with less than six months of experience.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders with less than six months of experience.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen to riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle. Always be extra careful when riding a new or unfamiliar motorcycle.

questions.question: In Illinois, what is allowed on a motorcycle?

options.text: A modified muffler that makes it louder.
Handlebars higher than the rider's head.
A blue license plate light.
A seat designed for two people.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat designed for two people.
questions.explanation: In Illinois, all motorcycles must have a white license plate light. Loud mufflers are not allowed. Handlebars must not be higher than the rider's head when sitting normally. A second rider is only allowed if the motorcycle and seat are designed for two people.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Roll on the throttle.
Hold the handlebars loosely.
Gently use the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to get off the road faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently use the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while riding, ease off the throttle and ride straight as you slow down. If you need to brake, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: When can a motorcycle pass on the right?

options.text: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
By riding on the shoulder of the road.
By riding on level grass.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right only if there is at least eight feet of clear pavement to the right of the vehicle you are passing. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: In Illinois, what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) means a person is legally intoxicated?

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.explanation: Under Illinois law, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to ride a motorcycle while intoxicated.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Kick the dog away.
Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Swerve around the dog.
Slow down as you approach, then speed up and pass it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach, then speed up and pass it.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If a dog chases you, slow down as you approach it. Then speed up and ride away from it.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Look to your left frequently.
Use your rearview mirrors more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay on the side of your lane away from the cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. If traffic is coming toward you, stay in the center of your lane instead.

questions.question: Where should you ride so the driver ahead can see you in their rearview mirror?

options.text: In the center of your lane.
In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane behind a car. This position appears in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: What does Illinois law require about motorcycle headlights?

options.text: Use the headlight at all times.
Use the headlight only between dusk and sunrise.
Use the headlight only when there is no bright sunlight.
Turn off the headlight when stopped in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlight at all times.
questions.explanation: Illinois law requires you to use your headlight at all times while riding. All motorcycles sold in the United States since 1978 have headlights that turn on automatically when the engine runs.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining in the body.
